revision_date: Current 2024 codification reviewed with the 2025–2026 enacted session
uas_topic: Privacy; imaging; mapping; surveying; utilities; transportation
regulated_party: Any UAS operator capturing images in Tennessee
regulated_activity: Capturing and using UAS imagery for commercial, professional, public, utility, mapping, surveying, transportation, or emergency purposes
requirement_type: Enumerated lawful-image categories and use limitation
permit_or_approval_required: No separate state permit stated; category-specific consent, credential, contract, or FAA authority may be required
summary: Section 39-13-902 makes UAS image capture lawful for enumerated purposes that include mapping; surveying by a duly registered land surveyor; utility operations, inspection, vegetation management, routing, and siting; owner or lawful-occupant consent; public-property imagery; pipeline work; FAA-authorized commercial services; TDOT planning, design, construction, maintenance, and operations; and certified photogrammetric mapping. Images may be used only for the lawful purpose for which they were captured. Incidental images of private persons or property from specified categories remain subject to § 39-13-905.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Use a mission-specific collection plan for Statewide that limits camera angle, dwell time, audio, zoom, thermal capture, and retention to the contracted purpose. Brief the crew on aborting or redirecting collection when people, residences, or unrelated activity enter the sensor footprint.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: N/A — no procurement or equipment-selection implication identified
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Preserve the mission purpose, property or participant permissions, sensor settings, collection boundary, retention rule, access log, and deletion record relevant to Tenn. Code Ann. § 39-13-902(a), (b). Escalate before using zoom, audio, thermal, recognition, persistent tracking, or secondary data uses that materially expand the agreed collection.
verification_status: Verified against the full current legal text and cross-checked against official TDOT UAS guidance
notes: The Tennessee code is difficult to retrieve section-by-section from an official current website. The complete section was reviewed on Justia and cross-checked against official Tennessee legislative and TDOT materials. This row does not treat the lawful-purpose list as an exemption from other state, property, or federal requirements.

revision_date: Current 2024 codification reviewed with the 2025–2026 enacted session
uas_topic: Privacy; surveillance; image use; data governance
regulated_party: Any person capturing, possessing, disclosing, displaying, distributing, or using UAS imagery

requirement_type: Criminal prohibition, destruction defense, and disclosure/evidentiary limits
permit_or_approval_required: Owner or lawful-occupant consent or another § 39-13-902 category may establish lawful capture
summary: Subject to § 39-13-902, § 39-13-903 prohibits capturing an image of an individual or privately owned real property with intent to conduct surveillance and knowingly using an image for a prohibited purpose. Section 39-13-904 separately penalizes possession and disclosure or use of an unlawfully captured image, with each image a separate offense and prompt-cessation or destruction defenses. Section 39-13-905 generally makes unlawful or qualifying incidental imagery unavailable in proceedings, public-records disclosure, discovery, or subpoena, except when used to prove a violation of the UAS-surveillance part.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Use a mission-specific collection plan for Statewide that limits camera angle, dwell time, audio, zoom, thermal capture, and retention to the contracted purpose. Brief the crew on aborting or redirecting collection when people, residences, or unrelated activity enter the sensor footprint.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: N/A — no procurement or equipment-selection implication identified
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Retain the current application, all attachments, written approval, conditions, amendments, and closeout records under Tenn. Code Ann. §§ 39-13-903(a)(1)–(2), 39-13-904, 39-13-905; a client's verbal direction should not substitute for the named authority's authorization. Escalate if the approving official, property boundary, operating dates, data rights, insurance terms, or ability to use a contractor is unclear.

notes: Section 39-13-905 limits disclosure and evidentiary use; it does not state a general deletion deadline for ordinary commercial mapping or surveying imagery. Section 39-13-904 sets Class C and Class B misdemeanor levels for possession and disclosure/use, respectively.

uas_topic: Events; fireworks; image capture; payload delivery

requirement_type: Criminal prohibition unless owner or operator consents
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — venue or fireworks-event owner/operator consent for the covered conduct
summary: Without the venue owner or operator’s consent, § 39-13-903 prohibits intentionally capturing an image of a person or event at, or dropping any item or substance into, an open-air venue where more than 100 people are gathered for a ticketed event. It also prohibits knowingly operating within or over a designated fireworks discharge site, display site, or fallout area during the event without the event owner or operator’s consent. Following the July 1, 2026 renumbering, these remain Class C misdemeanor provisions.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Map the event or fireworks perimeter and active time window for Statewide, obtain any consent expressly available under the rule, and keep launch, route, return-to-home, and contingency areas outside the covered zone unless authorized. Recheck the event schedule immediately before flight because setup, rehearsal, or ignition activity can change the applicable operating boundary.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: Use configuration-controlled payload interfaces and maintain documentation showing the purpose, operating limits, release safeguards, aircraft weight, and approved mission configuration. Avoid buying or fielding attachments whose capability could place an otherwise ordinary mapping aircraft within a weapon, projectile, contraband-delivery, or regulated dispensing provision.
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Retain the current application, all attachments, written approval, conditions, amendments, and closeout records under Tenn. Code Ann. § 39-13-903(a)(3)–(4), (b); a client's verbal direction should not substitute for the named authority's authorization. Escalate if the approving official, property boundary, operating dates, data rights, insurance terms, or ability to use a contractor is unclear.
verification_status: Verified against the full statute and the 2026 enacted renumbering
notes: The statute defines the covered fireworks areas. The school-ground amendment renumbered later subdivisions but did not alter these event and fireworks requirements.

regulated_activity: Using a drone to search for evidence or obtain information or data

permit_or_approval_required: Search warrant unless a recognized or enumerated statutory exception applies
commercial_operator_relevance: High when acting for a law-enforcement client
summary: Section 39-13-609 treats covered law-enforcement drone collection as a search and requires FAA compliance plus a warrant or recognized exception, unless an enumerated path applies. Those paths include specified threats, imminent danger, fugitive or hostage operations, missing-person searches, public-area crash investigation, crimes on public property, fire investigation, consent-based event security, declared natural disasters, and crime-scene investigation. Collected data generally must be deleted within 15 business days unless directly relevant to the lawful mission, investigation, or prosecution. Violations can trigger exclusion, destruction, damages, injunctions, and attorney fees.

Define in the scope and flight plan who authorizes the mission, controls the aircraft, receives the data, and is responsible for the cited records or use restrictions.
